A chain wears out much faster when it is left dry because the lubricant inside the chain relies on moisture to function properly. When the chain dries out, the metal components begin to rub against each other directly, causing friction, wear, and premature deterioration of the chain links and rollers. This accelerated wear leads to a shorter lifespan for the chain and requires more frequent replacement, which is costly for the shop and inconvenient for the customer.
